To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the resolvase protein binds to DNA and catalyzes site-specific recombination.

(1) resolvase forms an asymmetric dimer in the DNA-bound form, (2) the DNA-bound dimer is a tetramer, (3) the DNA-bound tetramer is a dimer of dimers, (4) the DNA-bound resolvase tetramer has an active site, and (5) the resolvase active site is a pocket formed between two monomers.
the recombination protein resolvase binds DNA in a sequence-specific manner and catalyzes the recombination reaction by binding to the DNA and forming a nucleoprotein complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of nucleoprotein complexes.
the structure and function of proteins that are involved in DNA replication, recombination and repair.
the molecular mechanisms of site-specific DNA recombination, the process by which DNA sequences are exchanged between two DNA duplexes in a sequence-specific fashion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DNA binding site of the recombination protein resolvase is a complex structure with a central DNA sequence element that is recognized and bound by the resolvase monomers and a flanking DNA element that is bound by the resolvasome.
the recombination process is a complex one, involving a number of steps.
resolvase binds to DNA in two steps: first, a specific interaction with the half-site DNA sequence, and then an interaction with the other half-site DNA sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have made progress in understanding the structure and mechanism of the site-specific DNA recombination enzyme resolvasse, and that we have also made progress in understanding how this protein recognizes and binds DNA, and how it is able to carry out its catalytic function.
we have made a major advance in our ability to understand how proteins interact with DNA.
we have shown the importance of the protein backbone and the role of the DNA in determining the structure and function of the complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resolvase-DNA complexes are dynamic and can adopt different conformations, and the DNA can be bent in different directions.
the protein is a very flexible molecule that is capable of interacting with DNA in many ways.

the DNA-binding domains of resolvase, which are structurally similar to the DNA-binding domains in other proteins that interact with DNA, can be used to understand the interaction between resolvase and the specific DNA sequences that it targets.
